# Quotation review

Read the complete artifact and supplied guidance. Resolved genre: case-study. Resolved language: en_US.

## Finding 1: Unclear subject of starting

- **Exact passage:** “I would set that time aside before the next building starts.”
- **Applicable requirement:** Keep terminology and reference clear; use natural American syntax. The case-study guidance specifically requires checking quoted speech for missing referents and clarifying only what the surrounding text settles.
- **What the reader loses:** A building does not itself start. The reader must reconstruct what will start there. The account concerns a trial of a shared repair log and its possible expansion, so the intended activity is recoverable, but the compressed wording obstructs the sentence's reference.
- **Smallest supported repair:** “I would set that time aside before the trial starts in the next building.” This makes the activity explicit while preserving the speaker's conditional advice and the preparation reservation. It does not assert that expansion has been decided.

No other concrete idiom, reference, or clarity obstructions found in the quoted statements. The second quotation's qualified appraisal functions as written.

# Quotation verification

Completed an independent reading of both files in full, assessing both quotations in the context of the complete case study under the supplied en_US guidance.

No findings. Both quotations use functioning American English and have recoverable, clear references. In the first, “that time” refers to the time required to agree on the categories; the next building supplies the setting for the speaker’s preparation advice. In the second, “one view of the reports” refers to the shared repair log, and the extra preparation week expresses a clear qualification of the speaker’s positive appraisal. Neither quotation contains a concrete idiom, reference, or clarity obstruction warranting a repair.

No text was changed. General editorial review, source verification, and mechanics were outside this reading.
